messages.content: Write an announcement telling customers that a service is moving to a new platform next quarter. Around 250 words.

You didn't name the service, platform, or dates, so I've written it with bracketed placeholders you can fill in. Swap in real numbers wherever you can — the vague spots are the ones customers distrust.

---

**Subject: [Service] moves to [New Platform] in [Quarter]**

Hi [Name],

We're moving [Service] onto [New Platform] during [Quarter]. Here's what that means for you.

The short version: your account, your data, and your saved [reports/settings/workflows] come with you. You don't need to re-create anything. Login stays at [URL], and your existing credentials keep working.

We're doing this because [Old Platform] can't keep up with [specific limit — e.g. "concurrent exports above 200 rows/sec"]. On [New Platform], [specific gain — e.g. "exports finish in under 90 seconds instead of 12 minutes"], and we can finally ship [feature customers have asked for].

**What you need to do**

Nothing before [date]. On [migration date], we'll move accounts in batches, starting with [tier/region]. You'll get an email 72 hours ahead of your slot.

Two things worth checking now:

- If you use our API, [endpoint pattern] changes to [new pattern] on [date]. The old endpoints keep answering until [sunset date].
- If you've allowlisted our IPs, add [range] before [date].

**Downtime**

We expect [X minutes] per account, inside the [day, time window, timezone] maintenance window. Status updates go to [status page URL].

We know migrations go wrong sometimes. If something breaks, mail [support address] and put MIGRATION in the subject — those go to a dedicated queue through [end date].

Questions before then? Reply to this email. A person reads it.

[Name]
[Title]
